metadataReview.note: Reviewed whole-battle dates: 30–31 October 1813, explicitly recorded by the City of Hanau and the Bayerisches Armeemuseum object commentary published by HDBG. The latter distinguishes the 30 October breakthrough and the 31 October fighting against the French rear guard. The imported 31 October alone omits the opening day. Geographical uncertainty remains: the existing source coordinate is retained as an approximate Hanau town-area proxy, not a reviewed centre of the battlefield. The municipal museum places the principal field in present-day Lamboy-Tümpelgarten. A KulturRegion FrankfurtRheinMain exhibition catalogue also documents the recapture of Hanau and bombardment of its Vorstadt on 31 October; urban fighting therefore prevents treating every town-area location as unrelated. Neither source validates the exact retained point or provides a replacement coordinate.

equipmentIdentity.note: Marmont’s retrospective firsthand account, livre XVIII, describes French skirmishers from Victor and Macdonald’s troops at Hanau, supported by Old Guard battalions, as well as cavalry, artillery and later Italian troops. This establishes a French imperial infantry component without equating the mixed army with the Guard or with a single national contingent. The local participant ID, aggregate name, membership and CDB quantities remain unchanged. No infantry proportion or additional strength, casualty or death count is inferred.

note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 139, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Approve the whole two-day Hanau engagement after restoring 30–31 October 1813. Hanau’s municipal chronology identifies French versus Bavarian-Austrian troops under Wrede; the Haus der Bayerischen Geschichte record describes Wrede’s force confronting the French main army, followed by fighting against the French rear guard on 31 October. Its approximately 30000 allied personnel and French main army twice that size are an independent estimate, not exact confirmation of CDB90’s 40000/60000. Preserve the CDB90 distinction: defender code 1 initial 40000+reinforcements 0; attacker code 3 total engaged 60000=initial 30000+reinforcements 30000. This is a comparison over the full battle, not a claim that all 60000 French were present at the opening or simultaneously in the firing line. The local allied identity clarifies the aggregate BAV ARMY label without adding an Austrian count. CDB casualty estimates remain unchanged, with no deaths inferred. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name FR ARMY): The municipal chronology and HDBG identify Napoleon’s French main army on 30 October and the rear-guard fighting on 31 October. CDB90’s code 3 count covers the whole two-day engagement, not simultaneous opening strength. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name BAV ARMY): HDBG and the City of Hanau explicitly identify Wrede’s combined Bavarian-Austrian force. BAV ARMY remains in the raw CDB90 qualifiers as an aggregate command; no Austrian count is added. HDBG estimates the combined force at about 30000, whereas CDB90 retains 40000.

The shako and flintlock model represents a French infantry clothing family within the mixed imperial army at Hanau. It is not an Old Guard uniform, an Italian uniform or a reconstruction of every unit. Marmont’s numerical claims and judgments are not adopted. The opposing Bavarian–Austrian aggregate remains unsplit and receives no common uniform. The local participant ID, aggregate name, membership and CDB quantities remain unchanged. No infantry proportion or additional strength, casualty or death count is inferred.
